speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; could you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they are painful?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
REQUEST TEST: Serum_Electrophoresis
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Forearm_lesions, Oral_mucosa

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work and electrophoresis show normal readings. Have you noticed any skin sores or blisters in other areas, and do you have a history of autoimmune conditions like lupus or dermatomyositis?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your recent medication changes, did you notice the blisters and ulcers appeared shortly after starting captopril or stopping meloxicam? Also, when you mention pain during sexual intercourse, does this involve blistering or ulceration on your genital mucosa?

speaker: Patient
text: includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: SJS/TEN (Stevens-Johnson Syndrome/Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis) secondary to Captopril. The combination of recent captopril initiation, forearm blistering, and new-onset painful oral/genital mucosal ulcers is highly suggestive of a severe drug reaction, rather than herpes or pemphigus given the rapid onset and specific temporal relationship to the medication.
